status: Died in House Natural Resources and Environment Committee; last action was committee consideration 2026-04-28, no report issued; 2026 RS adjourned sine die 2026-06-01 with no further movement
key_provisions: Would define data centers at 100 MW or more, require water permits for facilities exceeding 100 million gallons per year, require quarterly water-use reports, require parish notice and public hearings before permits, and assign unique identifiers to data center permits.

status: Enacted as Act 730; signed by Governor 2024-06-19; effective 2024-07-01
key_provisions: Created state and local sales and use tax rebate framework for qualifying data center facilities and equipment; Governor's office identified Act 730 as the incentive expected to support Meta's Richland Parish project.

sponsors: Rep. Rodney Schamerhorn; Rep. Wilford Carter Sr.
status: Died in House Commerce Committee; last action was committee consideration 2026-04-21, no report issued; 2026 RS adjourned sine die 2026-06-01 with no further movement
key_provisions: Would define data centers at 50 MW or more of new or expanded electric demand and bar electric utilities from recovering data-center-related costs from household customers.

status: Adopted by House 93-0 on 2025-06-08; received by Senate same day but never brought up for concurrence -- returned to Senate calendar subject to call 2025-06-09 and died there when the 2025 RS ended
key_provisions: Would create a special task force to study interagency consultation for data centers and natural resource planning, including water and energy impacts.

status: Enacted as Act 36; signed by Governor 2025-06-04; effective 2025-08-01
key_provisions: Explicitly classified construction and operation of data centers and associated commercial operations as an industrial area; allowed industrial areas to use cooperative agreements to provide required services.
